walkthroughs.body_html:
Sociological Theories & Approaches — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sociological Theories & Approaches brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sociological Theories & Approaches.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who argued the family had become symmetrical in 1973?
options: Murdock
Parsons
Young and Willmott
Oakley

mcqs.q: Murdock (1949) identified how many family functions?

options: Ethnography is the study of different ethnic groups only.
Americans eating more burgers.
The literal spread of McDonald's restaurants worldwide.
The spread of fast-food principles (efficiency, calculability, predictability, control) across society.

mcqs.q: How did Marx define social class?
options: Marx defined class by how much money people earn.
By relationship to the means of production: the bourgeoisie own productive resources; the proletariat sell their labour. Class is a structural relationship, not just income level.
Marx defined class by occupational status like the Registrar General.
Ethnography is the study of different ethnic groups only.
An in-depth qualitative method involving prolonged immersion in a community or setting to understand it from the inside — yielding rich descriptive data about culture, meaning and interaction.
Ethnography is the same as a written survey of a community.
Ethnography is the study of different ethnic groups only.
Americans eating more burgers.
